findings.title: Critical security vulnerability affects OpenSSH on Alpine Linux systems | TLDR
findings.summary_md: TLDR reported on November 5, 2026 that OpenSSH 10.6p2 was released with a workaround for a critical vulnerability affecting Linux systems that use musl libc with PAM disabled, such as Alpine Linux. OpenSSH developer Damien Miller advised administrators of affected systems to immediately set PasswordAuthentication=no or disable SSH entirely.

findings.title: OpenSSH 10.6p2 Fixes Password Bypass on Alpine Linux
findings.summary_md: Privacy Affairs reported on November 5, 2026 that OpenSSH 10.6p2 was released with an emergency workaround for a critical flaw in sshd. On Linux systems built on the musl C library where sshd checks passwords itself instead of through PAM, accounts that should never accept a password accept any password longer than 256 characters.

findings.title: OpenSSH and Alpine Linux warn of severe but niche bug | heise online
findings.summary_md: Heise Online reported on November 5, 2026 that OpenSSH and Alpine Linux warned of a severe but niche authentication-bypass bug affecting Linux systems using the musl C standard library without PAM. OpenSSH developer Damien Miller warned users of affected systems to disable password-based login immediately via PasswordAuthentication=no and restart sshd, or disable SSH altogether.

findings.title: Alpine OpenSSH Password Bypass: Update and Restart Now
findings.summary_md: fosslinux reported on November 5, 2026 that Alpine Linux's OpenSSH has a password bypass allowing an attacker who can reach the SSH port to log in with no password, and that fixed packages are available for every supported release back to version 3.16.

findings.title: OpenSSH flaw lets attackers log into password-disabled Linux accounts
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer reported on November 5, 2026 that security researcher Ozgün Kultekin of Wakefield disclosed and released details of an OpenSSH flaw dubbed *sshole that lets attackers log into password-disabled Alpine Linux and other musl-based accounts. Kultekin said the flaw has existed since 2016 and stems from how OpenSSH handles password verification errors.
